clean_story:
"Endless quantity. No largest number.
The word infinity comes from Latin infinitas, meaning without end, like a line that never stops.

Most think of infinity as just 'a lot.' But it’s more precise: it’s what happens when you keep counting and never reach a final number. Imagine a mirror facing another mirror—light bounces between them forever, never escaping. Infinity is the idea that this bouncing has no last reflection. In math, infinity isn’t a number but a concept: the set of all numbers goes on without bound. Yet not all infinities are equal. The infinity of whole numbers is smaller than the infinity of points on a line, even if both stretch forever. This was proven by Georg Cantor in 1874, using a method now called diagonalization. Infinity also appears in nature: fractals, like the jagged edge of a coastline, repeat their patterns at every scale, hinting at endless complexity. Three related subjects are fractal geometry, limits in calculus and infinite series."
